page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.48xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by 192 dedicated physical arm64 cores based on the AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.7 GHz, with 1 thread per core. The server includes 1536.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per core) and is equipped with 120000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 300 Gbps. The instance does not feature dedicated hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded processing and I/O capability. The instance achieves a top-tier stress-ng multi-core score of 311538.24 and Geekbench multi-core score of 19192.0, alongside top-tier results in Clang software compilation (85491.0) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (1368.05 GB/sec). Memory throughput is high, logging 895.12 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 410.26 GB/sec for writes. Database operations and in-memory key-value workloads also score in the top 10 percent, recording 356.82 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 46868.69 on PassMark database benchmarks.

Single-core performance is moderate, with Geekbench single-core at 1648.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1642.88 placing in the middle 50 percent. Workloads sensitive to single-threaded speed or requiring x86-specific instruction sets like AVX-512 will encounter architectural tradeoffs, and CPU-bound LLM prompt processing for small models tests in the bottom 25 percent. However, the high core density paired with massive local NVMe storage and substantial network bandwidth provides strong qualitative resource efficiency for parallel data processing.

The hardware configuration makes AWS i8ge.48xlarge well suited for large-scale distributed databases, transactional storage systems, big data analytics, real-time caching, and high-throughput web serving pipelines.
